4 primary findings establish a direct molecular link

Evidence establishing a direct link describes chaperone, autophagy, ubiquitin ligase, ubiquitination. Regulators named across the evidence: STUB1, GPX4. This is what the literature supports, and it is not the same as the annotation that retrieved the pair.

SHARED_DOWNSTREAM_MECHANISM (retrieval INCORRECT_BUT_CONNECTION_REAL): 4 independent primary findings establish a direct molecular link between the two diseases' proteins or processes, independent of the annotation that retrieved the pair.

scoped_identities.rationale: Restricted to HGNC:11427, the causal basis of Cerebellar Ataxia-Hypogonadism Syndrome is the same as that of Autosomal Recessive Spinocerebellar Ataxia 16, which has no other cause. Within this scope the two labels describe one entity, so a relationship between them is not an independent cross-disease discovery. The broader entity has additional causes and remains distinct outside this scope.

alternative_explanations.description: The diseases share symptoms without sharing a cause. Clinical overlap is common between disorders of the same organ.
The same cell type or tissue is affected by unrelated processes. A vulnerable cell population appears in many unrelated disorders.
The shared process term is broad enough to cover mechanistically distinct branches, so the annotation matches while the biology does not.
The two labels describe one disease or one allelic spectrum, so the apparent connection is nomenclature rather than biology.
The shared feature is perturbed in opposite directions, which argues against functional equivalence.
The shared gene participates in many disorders, so sharing it describes a research area rather than a specific mechanism.
One disease is far better annotated than the other, so apparent similarity or difference may reflect curation rather than biology.
